steps.what: Examine the firearm's mechanical condition and perform authorised forensic restoration to recover identifying information such as serial numbers, recording actual observations under established laboratory procedures.
Consult the authorised firearms reference database {OTHER} and current applicable classification sources in {DOCS}; verify identifiers and record the source versions used for legal-status assessment.
Determine the supported mechanical findings and legal status within existing competence, resolving uncertain classification through the established specialist process.
Write and check the actual mechanical, restoration and identification findings, source references and limitations in the existing forensic case system {OTHER}.
Save the checked final firearms examination record in the forensic case system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Retain the authorised firearms reference tools and forensic case record in {OTHER}, with source documents in {DOCS}. Physical examination, reference lookup, classification and record writing have separate time shares; no additional labour-saving change is supported in this already configured scenario.
tasks.previous_blocker: Uncertain evidence and jurisdiction-specific classification demand competent examination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native reference lookup and case forms already support the administrative work; their runtime earns no new saving.
tasks.still_hard: Damage can leave identifiers or mechanical condition uncertain, and legal status depends on current applicable sources.
tasks.human_edge: State defensible conclusions and explicit limits rather than filling gaps in the evidence.

ambition.what: No new classification or evidence-release authority.

tasks.altitude: The same forensic examination duties and decision rights remain.

evidence.claim: Structured case records and reference lookup support forensic documentation without replacing the physical examination or classification judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is the authorised technician's examination and stored findings; this is not repair for use, case disclosure or a change to evidential procedures. Shares are a scenario, not measured labour.

The technician records case and evidence IDs, actual examination observations, recovered identifier with uncertainty, image references, method revision, classification source and version, and conclusion limitations in s1-s4. Authorised reference custodians supply existing source material; missing identifiers or references require manual investigation. No identifier is guessed.

Native case fields and database search are assumed already in use after considering record writing and lookup separately. No duplicate summary, new approval ceremony or new inventory duty is invented.

The ordinary author check in s4 binds the exact final s5 record. Changes invalidate approval. Existing independent verification and jurisdiction-specific legal review remain unchanged. No new tool means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual native case and reference configuration
research_questions: Is any repeat transcription demonstrably outside the existing case form?

already_counted.description: Write and check the completed examination record.

incremental.description: No new tool or changed workflow to maintain.

approvals.approved_version: Final firearms examination record checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Physical examination, existing reference lookup, legal-status judgement, record writing and save all retain full time. No new labour-saving mechanism is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse digital evidence within the authorised case scope

steps.what: Verify the authorised examination scope, supplied forensic image or digital-media copy, integrity record and extraction limitations before analysis in the digital forensic analysis software {OTHER}.

Configure native file-type filters, explicit date ranges, hash grouping and timeline views in the digital forensic analysis software {OTHER}; inspect coverage and source locations rather than repeatedly navigating the same files.

Analyse the computer or digital-media records for evidence related to criminal activity; inspect source content, timestamps, attribution uncertainties and competing explanations, including material outside the initial filters when warranted.

Write and check the final analytical findings, source paths, filter provenance and limitations in the existing forensic case system {OTHER}, preserving the distinction between observed records and inferred activity.
Commit the checked final digital analysis record to the forensic case system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure saved analysis views in the existing digital forensic analysis software {OTHER} before considering custom processing. Explicit filters and hash groups reduce repeated navigation while preserving every source occurrence; the technician determines evidential meaning and writes the final record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated file navigation and rebuilding the same timeline views consumed operator time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forensic tools can reuse explicit filter settings, source-linked timelines and hash groups.
tasks.still_hard: Clock errors, shared devices, incomplete extraction and ambiguous authorship require careful interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a stored digital artefact from evidence that a particular person performed an act.

ambition.what: Test an alternative event chronology against the same preserved source records.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated navigation leaves more time for conflicting evidence; investigative authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Check reproducibility of an analytical result

evidence.claim: Native digital forensic analysis tools can retain source-linked filtered views, timelines and hash groups.

assumptions: Boundary starts with a supplied forensic copy and ends with the stored analysis record. Seizure, acquisition, independent review and external disclosure are separate unchanged tasks. Shares are an adoption scenario.

The existing acquisition process supplies evidence ID, copy reference, integrity value, acquisition time and extraction status. The technician verifies these in s1 and captures search terms, scope limits, timezone assumptions, date ranges, file-type rules and view version in s2. Missing metadata is resolved manually or recorded as a limitation; no free extraction work is added.

Native configuration is tested first. Only repeated operator navigation and view setup lose time. Indexing runtime earns no labour saving. Hash grouping never deletes occurrences or hides their paths; search coverage and meaning remain human checks.
No model infers criminality, identity or relevance. s4's ordinary author check binds the final record for s5; edits invalidate it. No access beyond the authorised case scope is introduced.
unknowns: Existing saved-view use and operator navigation time
Completeness of supplied forensic copies and timestamp metadata
research_questions: Can native views retain every grouped occurrence and reproduce the exact filter settings?

already_counted.description: Set and check analysis views, source locations and filter coverage.

incremental.description: Validate saved-view behaviour after parser or tool updates.

approvals.approved_version: Final digital analysis record and source references checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where repeated navigation and view setup occupy 25 hours, native reuse removes 40%: 10 gross hours less 2 upkeep. Zero where already configured. Source verification, interpretation, final record writing and commit remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician keeps forensic interpretation and evidence responsibilities; native analysis views reduce repeated digital navigation only.
reach: Review analytical traceability with quality control analysts
role.ambitious_version: Test competing evidential explanations against preserved source records without delegating forensic conclusions to software.
